name: stack-trace
title: Stack Trace
description: A compact error panel showing the error type and message with copy and expand controls. Opening it lists each call frame and greys out library and runtime internals.
use: A developer tool or assistant answer needs to show a real runtime error without dumping raw text.
avoid: It is dense monospace content for developers, the message truncates, and it wants a wide container.
a11y: The copy and chevron controls are icon-only with no accessible names, so screen readers hear bare buttons. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A wide dark rounded panel. Its header pairs a small warning triangle, a red error type, a white message and two icon buttons; expanded, a bordered body underneath lists monospace frames line by line.
behaves: Clicking the header or the chevron unfolds the frame list with a fade and flips the chevron. The copy button writes the raw trace to the clipboard and briefly shows a tick, while frames from node_modules and node internals sit dimmed.
customise: The raw trace string, open state and a file-path click handler are props; the header, body and buttons are assembled from the exported sub-parts.
weight: light: A parsed string and a short list of frame rows behind one fade and border transition.
demo: Fake TypeError about reading 'lineItems' during checkout, with seven frames across app and node_modules files.
issues: The message is cut with an ellipsis, so a long error can never be read in full from the header.
polishWhy: Clear hierarchy and dimmed internal frames; truncated message and unnamed icons hold it back.

props.name: onFilePathClick
props.type: (filePath: string, line?: number, column?: number) => void
